title: Stock Trading With a Rest Day
statement:
`prices[i]` is the price of a stock on day `i`. You can buy and sell as often as you like, but with these rules: you hold **at most one share** at a time (sell before you buy again), and **after you sell you must wait one full day** before you can buy again (you cannot buy on the day right after a sale). Buying and selling on the same day is not allowed.

Return the **largest total profit**.

examples.explanation: Skip the first two days, buy at 2 on day 2, sell at 10 on day 4: profit 8. (Selling at 8 on day 1 and trading again leaves day 2 as the rest day, which only allows a profit of 6.)
Prices only fall: do not trade.

hints.nudge: At the end of each day you are in one of three situations: holding a share, just sold it today, or free to buy (holding nothing and not just sold). What can each situation turn into the next day?
hints.pattern: Dynamic programming with three states per day: hold, sold (just sold today) and rest (nothing in hand, free to buy).
hints.pseudocode:
hold = -infinity; sold = 0; rest = 0
for price in prices:
  previousSold = sold
  sold = hold + price            (sell today)
  hold = max(hold, rest - price) (keep, or buy today from a free state)
  rest = max(rest, previousSold) (stay free, or become free after yesterday's sale)
return max(sold, rest)
hints.walkthrough: Trying every buy/sell plan is exponential. Describe the end of each day by one of three states and keep the best profit for each: `hold` (you own a share), `sold` (you sold it today, so tomorrow you cannot buy), and `rest` (you own nothing and may buy tomorrow). Transitions: to hold today you either held yesterday, or bought today from rest (not from sold: that is the cooldown); to be in sold today you must have held yesterday and sell at today's price; to be in rest today you either rested yesterday or were in sold yesterday (the rest day has passed). Update the three values for every price, using yesterday's `sold` for the rest update. The answer is the best of sold and rest on the last day (holding a share at the end is never better). O(n) time, O(1) memory.
